name: Melapress Role Editor
author: Melapress

sections.description:
Melapress Role Editor enables you to easily manage your WordPress user roles. Create, edit, and delete user roles like a pro thanks to the intuitive interface and wizards that hand-hold you every step of the way.

Melapress Role Editor comes with several features, including:
* Ability to create, edit, and delete custom user roles with ease
* Useful out-of-the-box custom roles
* Backup and restore user role configurations
* Auto-detect user role changes with restore prompt
* Add users to multiple roles
* Allow or Deny capabilities
* Out-of-the-box support for Easy Digital Downloads, WooCommerce, and Yoast SEO
* Capability of pretty names for easier referncing

Melapress Role Editor Benefits

Stress-free configuration with step-by-step wizards

Melapress Role Editor makes it easy to manage roles thanks to its intuitive interface and wizards that walk you through the entire process. By using wizards, you can rest easy knowing that all necessary steps have been accounted for and nothing was missed. Of course, you can also edit roles manually if you wish.

Increased security with auto change detection

Melapress Role Editor keeps a record of each role’s capabilities for security and reliability. It alerts you whenever there is a change so that you can choose to restore roles to the previous configuration or accept the changes, keeping you in the driver’s seat at all times.

Peace of mind with backups and restore

Not sure if planned role changes will pan out? Don’t worry – simply take a backup of the existing configuration from within the plugin so that you can always restore a known working configuration should something break.

Better guidance with out-of-the-box custom roles

Melapress Role Editor comes with a number of pre-configured roles designed to help you get started quickly. Modeled after common roles in the WordPress business such as Business owner, Developer, and HR manager, each role has been designed to respect the principle of least privilege while giving you a head start in configuring new custom roles.

Simplify complexity with multiple roles and capability deny

WordPress environments can get pretty complex, so we added features to accomodate every scenario. You can assign users multiple roles to avoid creating additional roles. You can also explicity deny capabilities to ensure the utmost level of security in complex scenarios.

MAINTAINED & SUPPORTED BY MELAPRESS

Melapress builds high-quality niche WordPress security & management plugins, including WP Activity Log, WP 2FA, Melapress Login Security, and others.

Visit the Melapress website for more information about the company and the plugins it develops.

Install the plugin from within WordPress

Managing roles is easy with Melapress Role Editor. Simply:

  1. Navigate to Plugins > Add New, from your WordPress dashboard
  2. Search for Melapress Role Editor
  3. Install & activate Melapress Role Editor from your Plugins page

Install the plugin manually (via file upload)

  1. Download the plugin from the WordPress plugins repository
  2. Unzip the zip file and upload the folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory
  3. Activate melapress Role Editor through the Plugins page in WordPress

sections.faq:
Is Melapress Role Editor free?

Yes, Melapress File Monitor is a 100% free plugin.

Does the plugin send any data to Melapress?

No, the plugin does not send any data to us whatsoever.

Is Melapress Role Editor easy to use?

Melapress Role Editor has been designed from the ground up with ease of use in mind. You’ll find wizards to walk you through configuration processes, pre-configured roles to help you get started easily and quickly, and many other features to help you make the most out of the plugin.

Does Melapress Role Editor allow you to set different permissions for each role?

Yes, each role is fully customizable so that you can set whichever capabilities you want that role to have. Furthermore, you can explicitly allow or deny capabilities to ensure .
sections.changelog:
1.4.0 (2026-10-30)

  • Security fixes

    • Fixed a broken access control vulnerability affecting versions 1.3.0 and earlier, reported by Peter Tang.
    • Fixed a privilege escalation vulnerability affecting versions 1.3.0 and earlier, reported by Peter Tang.

  • Functionality & plugin improvements

    • Added WordPress.org Live Preview support for the free edition through WordPress Playground.
    • Updated the minimum required WordPress version to 6.0.
    • Updated the minimum required PHP version from 8.0 to 8.1.
    • Changed the plugin description displayed on the WordPress Plugins page.
    • Improved overall plugin security and stability, with additional hardening and minor bug fixes.

1.3.0 (2026-06-09)

  • New features

    • Added Secondary Role support for invited network users.
    • Added a deactivation feedback form to assist with user feedback collection.

  • Bug fixes

    • Fixed alignment and styling issues in the plugin UI caused by changes introduced in WordPress Core 7.
    • Fixed: PHP Notice raised by WordPress Core 7 where WP_Scripts::add was being called incorrectly.
    • Fixed: Posts menu item incorrectly shown in wp-admin for users or roles with page-only permissions.
    • Fixed: Role not being created when clicking “Skip the wizard” in the Add New User Role wizard before completing all steps.
    • Fixed: Plugin data removal during uninstallation not working correctly – removal now completes as expected.

  • Plugin & functionality improvements

    • Removed deprecated WordPress core capabilities from the plugin codebase, eliminating redundant and obsolete code.
    • Replaced the Search button with a placeholder in the first-time setup wizard for improved consistency.
    • Role type labels on the role listing page have been simplified for clarity.
    • Code and architecture improvements across multiple classes for improved consistency and maintainability.

1.2.0 (2026-01-14)

  • Security fix

    • Improper Authorization to Authenticated (Subscriber+) Privilege Escalation via Secondary Role Assignment.

  • Improvements

    • Removed redundant Search button from Role Editor as search runs automatically while typing.
    • Improved the UX: added notes and description on core roles, and also restricted deletion of core roles.

  • Bug fixes

    • Users with post-specific edit permissions can now publish changes directly instead of being forced to submit a post for review.

1.0.1 (2024-02-26)

  • Improvements

    • On multisite networks, the plugin now correctly displays the “Super Admin” role for relevant users when they are looked up/filtered through the plugin.
    • Improved various UI elements across plugin pages and adjusted help text descriptions.
    • Added missing help text for the custom “Content Editor” role created by the plugin.

  • Bug fixes

    • Fixed restricted plugin pages for admins on multisite networks.
    • Multisite: Resolved an issue preventing users from being added with both a primary and secondary role on a subsite.
    • Fixed a bug where users with multiple roles and overlapping capabilities were not following the “DENY” rule correctly.
